title: An optimized protocol for the isolation of rare stromal cell populations from the mouse spleen
protocol: Euthanize mice using either CO2 or other approved methods.
Lay euthanized mice on their right flank and spray body area with 70% ethanol.
Using scissors, cut through the skin and peritoneum to expose the spleen.
Harvest the spleen with forceps and place individual spleens in 1–2 mL of harvest media and keep on ice.
Remove external tissue connected to the spleen.
Place one spleen in the middle of a Petri dish.
Load two 1 mL syringes equipped with 26G needles with digestion media.
Inject 2 mL of digestion media evenly across the spleen, injecting around 200 μL in one area and repeating until the entire spleen is injected.
Transfer the spleen and digestion media into a 15 mL tube.
Incubate tubes in a pre-warmed water bath set to 37°C for 30 min.
Remove tubes from the water bath and place them back at 20°C–22°C.
Thoroughly gently mix spleens using a 1 ml pipette, mixing 90 times.
Digest spleens completely until no fragments are left.
Leave undisturbed if any tissue fragments remain, allowing them to settle at the bottom of the tube.
Transfer supernatant into a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL of FACS buffer without disturbing settled pieces.
Repeat digestion by adding 1 mL of digestion media to remaining spleen fragments and incubate for 15 min at 37°C.
Digest spleens until no visible tissue remains, then transfer supernatant from second digestion into the first fraction's tube containing FACS buffer.
Add 14 mL of FACS buffer to each digested spleen sample and centrifuge for 5 min at 500 × g, 4°C.
Remove supernatant and perform red blood cell lysis by resuspending cells with 1 mL of RBC lysis buffer.
Incubate for 2 minutes at 20°C-22°C to allow lysis buffer to act on the cells.
Wash cells by adding 10 mL of FACS buffer and centrifuge for 5 min at 500 × g, 4°C.
Remove supernatant after washing step and resuspend spleen cells in 5 mL of FACS buffer.
Filter cell suspension through a 75 μm nylon mesh into a new tube.
Centrifuge filtered cells for 5 min at 500 × g, 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant using a vacuum trap system to remove all excess liquid.
Add 250 μL of FACS buffer into each tube.
Add 35 μL of anti-mouse CD45 microbeads.
Resuspend cell pellets and incubate for 15 min on ice.
Wash cells by adding 5 mL of FACS buffer.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 500 × g at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant using a vacuum trap.
Resuspend cells in 500 μL of FACS buffer.
Keep cells on ice.
Attach the QuadroMACS Separator to the MACS MultiStand.
Place an LS Column in the separator for each spleen sample.
Prepare the LS Column by rinsing with 3 mL of FACS buffer.
Let the buffer run through the column.
Wait until the buffer has completely run through and remove the reservoir.
Place a 10 or 15 mL collection tube under the LS Column.
Apply the spleen cell suspension onto the prepared LS Column.
Add 500 μL of FACS buffer to the tube containing the cell suspension.
Collect any remaining cells from the supernatant and apply it onto the column.
Once the buffer has completely run through, wash the column once with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Wash the column two more times with 3.5 mL of FACS buffer each time.
The total volume in the collection tube should be 9 mL.
Put the collection tubes on ice.
Remove the column from the QuadroMACS Separator and flush with FACS buffer into a separate tube to collect the CD45+ cell fraction.
Stain enriched stromal cells with antibodies in FACS tubes or round-bottom 96-well plates for phenotyping.
Use one spleen per staining when analyzing mouse white pulp stromal cells due to low subset numbers.
Discriminate live versus dead cells using bright markers such as DAPI or Propidium Iodide (PI).
Add Zombie fixable viability dye directly into the surface stain cocktail mix if intracellular staining is required.
Include counting beads just before acquisition in each sample for cellularity enumeration.
Manually count samples if not using counting beads for cellularity analysis.
Take a 500 μL aliquot of unstained stromal cells from each sample, pool together and set aside.
Centrifuge remaining cells for 5 min, 500 × g, 4°C.
Remove supernatant, resuspend stromal cells in 1 mL of FACS buffer and transfer into FACS tubes.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min, 500 × g, 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend each sample with 100 μL of stromal cell cocktail mix 1, made in FACS buffer.
Incubate cells for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Wash cells by adding 1 mL of FACS buffer and centrifuge cells for 5 min at 500 × g, 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells with 100 μL stromal cell cocktail mix 2 made in FACS buffer.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Wash cells by adding 1 mL of FACS buffer and centrifuge cells for 5 min, 500 × g, 4°C.

Prepare Fixation/Permeabilization buffer by diluting 1 part of the Fixation/Permeabilization Concentrate with 3 parts of Fixation/Permeabilization Diluent from the eBioscience Foxp3/Transcription Factor staining buffer set.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min, 500 × g, at 4°C, aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μL of Fixation/Permeabilization working solution.
Incubate cells for 45 min at 20°C–22°C, in the dark.

Prepare a 1× working solution of Permeabilization Buffer by mixing 1 part of 10× Permeabilization Buffer from the eBioscience Foxp3/Transcription Factor staining buffer set with 9 parts of distilled water.
Wash cells by adding 1 ml of Permeabilization Buffer and centrifuge cells for 5 min, 500 × g, at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μL of intracellular antibody mix diluted in Permeabilization buffer.
Incubate cells for 45 min at 4°C and in the dark.
Wash cell by adding 1 ml of Permeabilization Buffer and centrifuge cells for 5 min, 500 × g, at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in 200 μL of FACS buffer.
Keep samples at 4°C and in the dark until acquisition of the flow cytometer.
Add 20 μl of 10 μg/ml PI or 20 μl of 5 μM DAPI to each sample.
Keep samples at 4°C and in the dark until acquisition of the flow cytometer.
Vortex the samples just prior to acquisition.
Add 20 μL of counting beads per sample.
Acquire samples on a FACS machine.
Sort populations of interest with a BD FACS Aria III for single cell RNA sequencing.
Use a 100 μm nozzle and 20 psi during sorting.
Do not exceed a speed rate of 5,000 events per second during sorting.
Sort cells directly in RPMI supplemented with 10% FBS.
Centrifuge the sorted cells following sorting.
Resuspend the cells in PBS with 0.01% BSA after centrifuging.
Perform single cell RNA sequencing according to manufacturer’s instructions.
